title: Sorted repeated-tuple contraction
statement: Let X be a scheme, I a linearly ordered type, U : I → Opens(X), F an abelian-group presheaf, and S the chosen Čech product complex over the terminal open. Let p ≥ 0, s be a degree-p cochain, and t a tuple of p+1 indices. The boundary of the repeated-tuple contraction on a nondecreasing tuple equals the section on repeated tuples and zero on strictly increasing tuples.

proof.text: A stable sorting permutation of a monotone tuple is monotone: any inversion forces equality of labels and contradicts stability. A monotone permutation of Fin is identity. Two first-repeat positions are equal because the earlier repeated equality contradicts the later position's strict prefix. Reduce the explicit sorting homotopy sum to its unique summand at the identity permutation and first repeat. On a strictly increasing tuple, and all its faces, the sum vanishes. The homotopy boundary formula therefore vanishes in this case, including degree zero.

For a non-strict monotone tuple, choose the least adjacent equality using Nat.find; monotonicity and minimality give its strict prefix. Degree zero is impossible. In positive degree expand the homotopy boundary as Kd+dK, reduce Kd to the unique first-repeat summand, and distribute the restriction homomorphism over the signed differential sum. Partition that sum into the three central positions and their complement. The central-face theorem gives s(t). In degree one, the complement is empty and K in degree zero is zero. In higher degrees, the outer-face theorem gives minus dK. Addition cancels dK, giving s(t), exactly the non-strict branch of the stated conclusion.

lean.statement: theorem cechSortedContraction (X : Scheme.{u}) {I : Type v} [LinearOrder I] (U : I → X.Opens) (F : X.Opensᵒᵖ ⥤ AddCommGrpCat.{w}) (S : SiteCechComplex U (fun i ↦ homOfLE (le_top : U i ≤ ⊤))) (p : ℕ) (s : S.cochains F p) (t : Fin (p + 1) → I) (ht : Monotone t) : ((Homotopy.nullHomotopicMap' (cechSecondSortingFamily X U F S)).f p) s t = s t - (if StrictMono t then s t else 0)
